name: Caséta Smart Dimmer PD-6WCL (US)

radios.note: The dimmer uses Lutron's own Clear Connect RF radio, which isn't Wi-Fi, Thread, Zigbee, Z-Wave or Bluetooth, so none of our radio values fit. The Smart Bridge (Smart Hub) talks to it over Clear Connect and joins your router by Ethernet.

matter.note: No Matter claim found on the Lutron pages we saw; not confirmed either way.

apple_home.note: Lutron lists Apple HomeKit (including Siri) among the features the Smart Hub adds, so the dimmer shows up in Apple Home through the bridge.

google_home.note: Lutron lists Google Home among the features the Smart Hub adds; it reaches the dimmer through the bridge.

alexa.note: Lutron lists Amazon Alexa among the features the Smart Hub adds; it needs the bridge.

smartthings.note: Lutron's support article adds Lutron as a partner in the SmartThings app; the Caséta hub must be connected and reachable in the Lutron app. It is a cloud-to-cloud link, and Pico remotes don't appear in SmartThings.

home_assistant.note: Home Assistant's Lutron Caséta integration connects to the Smart Bridge over the local network (local push).

hubRequired.note: Lutron says remote access, scenes, schedules and voice assistants need the Smart Bridge (now called Smart Hub). Without it the dimmer pairs only with Pico remotes and sensors.

localControl.note: Home Assistant's Lutron Caséta integration talks to the Smart Bridge over the local network (local push). Lutron's app, Alexa, Google Home and SmartThings links go through Lutron's cloud.

switchForm.note: Replaces a standard single-pole wall dimmer in a 1-gang US wallbox.

dimmer.note: Rated 150 W for dimmable LED and 600 W for incandescent or halogen.

neutralRequired.note: Two-wire design that installs like a regular switch. A ground wire is optional unless local code demands it.

gangs.note: Lutron's spec calls for a 1-gang US wallbox.

summary: The Lutron Caséta PD-6WCL replaces a standard single-pole dimmer in a 1-gang US wallbox, and its two-wire design needs no neutral. Apple Home, Google Home, Alexa and SmartThings all reach it through the Caséta Smart Bridge (now called Smart Hub); Home Assistant also connects to the bridge, over the local network. On its own it pairs only with Pico remotes and sensors. It dims 150 W of LED or 600 W of incandescent and halogen.
caveats: Needs the Caséta Smart Bridge (now called Smart Hub) for app, voice and ecosystem control; the bridge plugs into your router by Ethernet.
LED loads are limited to 150 W, and the bulbs must be dimmable.
